mechanism.base: Fire works metal, the old texts say: the forge softens the blade, and iron that held one shape for ages gives it up inside the heat. The flame does not break the ore, it loosens it until the hammer can ask for a new line. Every fire wants something hard to work on, and every finished blade keeps the warmth that once made it move.
mechanism.catalyst_turn: With too little Metal, the fire has nothing hard to work: heat spent on open air, light with no iron under it. Pick one solid thing and finish it this month.
mechanism.friction_turn: With too much Metal, the ore crowds the forge: more iron than the fire can soften, and the flame goes dim under the load. Set most of it aside and feed the fire first.

catalyst.clause: the fire has nothing hard to work: heat spent on open air, light with no iron under it
catalyst.remedy: Pick one solid thing and finish it this month.

friction.clause: the ore crowds the forge: more iron than the fire can soften, and the flame goes dim
friction.remedy: Set most of it aside and feed the fire first.

wide.clause: You have plenty of Metal, enough iron to keep the fire busy for years.
wide.remedy: Work it. Shape one real thing at a time.

missing.clause: No Metal in reach of the fire: light burning on the air, nothing hard to shape or keep.
missing.remedy: Borrow iron: one order to fill, one thing handed over finished.

spared.clause: No Metal to drain the fire, and the warmth stays with the one who carries it.
spared.remedy: Leave it. Keep the fire fed before taking on more.

thin.clause: Only a little Metal, one small piece of iron that the fire softens without going out.
thin.remedy: Keep it small. Finish what is in hand first.

excess.clause: Too much metal puts the fire out: more to shape than the heat can ever soften.
excess.remedy: Put most of it down. Fuel the fire before the work.

function.definition_catalyst: Your Action is what you go and build, claim and provide. Metal makes it exact, so what you take on ends finished or not at all. As a catalyst, you have more drive than work for it, and you chase the next opening more than you finish anything to keep.
function.definition_friction: Your Action is what you go and build, claim and provide. Under Metal it stays exact, and nothing you claim counts until it is finished. As a friction, you take on past your strength, and you start a new venture rather than keep the money and love already yours.
function.advise_catalyst: Your drive outruns the places you have to put it, and an opening you only look at becomes weight. Pick one venture and give it a finish date. Move a fixed sum into savings each month before you spend the rest. Tell the man who raised you one thing you built this year. Finish one small thing before bed.
function.advise_friction: Seek Fire, the Body energy. Fire is warmth kept in: fuel, rest, the light that keeps itself lit before it works on anything. Let it hold what Metal spends. You say yes to more than you can finish, and tired is where you make your worst deals. Sleep on any new venture before you answer. Eat lunch sitting down.

candidates.cta_verdict: Your drive goes wherever there is something hard to shape, and you finish more by picking one thing to provide for than by chasing every opening you spot.

mechanism.base: The refined prevails over the stubborn, and so fire works metal: in the furnace the hardest thing in the world goes soft, gives up its rock, and takes a finer form. Cold, metal refuses every argument. Heated, it flows like consent, and the smith reads the glow the way farmers read the sky.
mechanism.catalyst_turn: Run thin, the forge stands cold: heat with nothing hard to work, charm with no asset under it. Your chart asks you to work metal. Take on the difficult, valuable thing.
mechanism.friction_turn: Run heavy, the melting never stops: everything softened for reworking, nothing allowed to cool and keep an edge. Let finished things stay finished. A forge needs objects, not only fire.

catalyst.clause: The forge stands cold: heat with nothing hard to work, charm with no asset under it.
catalyst.remedy: Take on the difficult, valuable thing.

friction.clause: The melting never stops: everything softened for reworking, nothing allowed to cool and keep an edge.
friction.remedy: A forge needs objects, not only fire.

wide.clause: You are well supplied with Metal, the hard thing your heat was made to work.
wide.remedy: Work the hard, valuable thing in front of you.

missing.clause: The forge stands empty: heat with nothing hard to work.
missing.remedy: Borrow metal: one difficult, valuable thing.

spared.clause: Metal runs absent, and nothing needs reworking: the fire warms instead of melts.
spared.remedy: Keep it. Take hard work rarely, on purpose.

thin.clause: Metal runs thin and unwanted: a small piece, easily finished.
thin.remedy: Finish it and let it cool.

excess.clause: Too much metal puts out the fire: more hard work than the heat can take, effort cooling.

function.definition_catalyst: Metal is your Action, and as a catalyst, it is your heat applied to hard, valuable problems: negotiations, difficult skills, work that resists until it yields. Easy tasks waste you.
function.definition_friction: Metal is your Action, and as a friction, it is reworking what should be finished: renegotiating settled things, polishing shipped work, effort spent softening what was already solid. Done is a decision you keep reopening.
function.advise_catalyst: Difficulty is your natural price filter, so use it openly. Take the assignment everyone else avoids. Price your work higher than feels comfortable and let the discomfort season. Once a year, pick one skill hard enough to embarrass you for months.
function.advise_friction: Finished things are load-bearing, so stop testing them. Close three open loops this week and do not reopen them. Give every task a final pass, then a lock. Aim the reworking energy at one genuinely unsolved problem instead.

$original.cta_verdict: You act by forging, heat applied until something keeps its shape, and your money follows the finished piece rather than the bright idea.
